title: Odd Perfect Numbers
exact_target: Is any odd positive integer equal to the sum of its proper positive divisors?

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 1496 (NUM-002). CC BY 4.0.

Pascal Ochem and Joshua Zelinsky, \emph{On odd perfect numbers with exactly one even exponent greater than 2}, arXiv:2607.19746 (2026), Section 1, definition of an odd perfect number. The cited definition concerns all odd perfect numbers, independently of the paper's restricted factorization theorem.

John Cowles and Ruben Gamboa, \emph{Perfect Numbers in ACL2}, EPTCS 192 (2015), 53--59, DOI 10.4204/EPTCS.192.5; arXiv:1509.06081v1, Sections 1--2, the unrestricted infinitude question and $\sigma(n)=2n$ definition.
